limits: Only AMH sex comparison in minipuberty uses this policy; ordinary multiple-hormone views and puberty comparison keep their existing contracts.
The lines are medians of two separate infant population models, not paired observations, longitudinal mean trajectories, reference intervals or a diagnostic classification.
Both infant studies used serum and Access 2. The male model is an approximate figure digitization; the female model comes from the published table.
No extrapolation to birth and no older-child model is joined at the first birthday. The common curve domain is distinct from an individual patient's unchanged source eligibility.
A qualified seven-day boy may have his own Busch reference marker before the common curve starts at 0.02 years. Neither sex receives a numeric comparison point at exactly one year.
The fixed logarithmic axis expresses concentration ratios. Its bounds are presentation choices, not normal ranges or assay detection limits.
Zero and results below the axis use a downward arrow; results above the axis use an upward arrow. Neither is placed as an exact result circle at the log boundary.
Source points, domains, unit factors and laboratory interpretation remain unchanged.
